passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the whole congregation of Israel and tell them: Be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to all the people of Israel.
The LORD told Moses to say this to them.
The LORD is holy.
The LORD is their God.
The LORD told the people to be holy.
The LORD told them to be holy because He is holy.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־ כָּל־ עֲדַ֧ת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֥ אֲלֵהֶ֖ם קְדֹשִׁ֣ים תִּהְי֑וּ כִּ֣י קָד֔וֹשׁ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Each of you must respect his mother and father, and you must keep My Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God is the LORD your God.
God commands you to respect your mother.
God commands you to respect your father.
God commands you to keep His Sabbaths.
passages.original: אִ֣ישׁ אִמּ֤וֹ וְאָבִיו֙ תִּירָ֔אוּ וְאֶת־ שַׁבְּתֹתַ֖י תִּשְׁמֹ֑רוּ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Do not turn to idols or make for yourselves molten gods. I am the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God is the LORD.
God is their God.
Do not turn to idols.
Do not make molten gods for yourselves.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּפְנוּ֙ אֶל־ הָ֣אֱלִילִ֔ים וֵֽאלֹהֵי֙ מַסֵּכָ֔ה לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ לָכֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: When you sacrifice a peace offering to the LORD, you shall offer it for your acceptance.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God commands the people of Israel.
You must bring a peace offering to the LORD.
You must offer the peace offering in a way that pleases God.
You must offer it so that God will accept it.
passages.original: וְכִ֧י תִזְבְּח֛וּ זֶ֥בַח שְׁלָמִ֖ים לַיהוָ֑ה לִֽרְצֹנְכֶ֖ם תִּזְבָּחֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it, or on the next day; but what remains on the third day must be burned up.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws about sacrifices.
God required peace offerings to be eaten soon after sacrifice.
You must eat the sacrifice on the day you offer it.
You may also eat it on the next day.
If any of the sacrifice remains until the third day, you must burn it in the fire.
passages.original: בְּי֧וֹם זִבְחֲכֶ֛ם יֵאָכֵ֖ל וּמִֽמָּחֳרָ֑ת וְהַנּוֹתָר֙ עַד־ י֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י בָּאֵ֖שׁ יִשָּׂרֵֽף׃

passages.text: If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is tainted and will not be accepted.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws about peace offerings.
A peace offering is a sacrifice to the LORD.
God commanded that people must eat the peace offering on the day it is sacrificed or on the next day.
If anyone eats any of the offering on the third day, that meat is tainted.
God will not accept the offering if it is eaten on the third day.
passages.original: וְאִ֛ם הֵאָכֹ֥ל יֵאָכֵ֖ל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י פִּגּ֥וּל ה֖וּא לֹ֥א יֵרָצֶֽה׃

passages.text: Whoever eats it will bear his iniquity, for he has profaned what is holy to the LORD. That person must be cut off from his people.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws about sacrifices.
God said some meat from sacrifices is holy.
If a person eats this meat on the third day, he does wrong.
This person will be guilty.
He has treated what is holy to the LORD as common.
He has profaned what belongs to God.
This person must be separated from his people.
passages.original: וְאֹֽכְלָיו֙ עֲוֺנ֣וֹ יִשָּׂ֔א כִּֽי־ אֶת־ קֹ֥דֶשׁ יְהוָ֖ה חִלֵּ֑ל וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵעַמֶּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: When you reap the harvest of your land, you are not to reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to the people of Israel.
God said, "When you harvest your land, do not reap to the very edges of your field."
Do not gather the leftover parts of your harvest.
Leave some of the crop in your field.
passages.original: וּֽבְקֻצְרְכֶם֙ אֶת־ קְצִ֣יר אַרְצְכֶ֔ם לֹ֧א תְכַלֶּ֛ה פְּאַ֥ת שָׂדְךָ֖ לִקְצֹ֑ר וְלֶ֥קֶט קְצִֽירְךָ֖ לֹ֥א תְלַקֵּֽט׃

passages.text: You must not strip your vineyard bare or gather its fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God gave them laws for their land.
God said, “Do not strip your vineyard bare.
Do not gather the fallen grapes from your vineyard.
Leave the grapes for the poor.
Leave the grapes for the foreigner.
I am the LORD your God.”
passages.original: וְכַרְמְךָ֙ לֹ֣א תְעוֹלֵ֔ל וּפֶ֥רֶט כַּרְמְךָ֖ לֹ֣א תְלַקֵּ֑ט לֶֽעָנִ֤י וְלַגֵּר֙ תַּעֲזֹ֣ב אֹתָ֔ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: You must not steal. You must not lie or deceive one another.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people.
God says, “Do not steal.”
God says, “Do not lie.”
God says, “Do not deceive one another.”
passages.original: לֹ֖א תִּגְנֹ֑בוּ וְלֹא־ תְכַחֲשׁ֥וּ וְלֹֽא־ תְשַׁקְּר֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲמִיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You must not swear falsely by My name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God is your God.
Do not swear falsely by God's name.
If you swear falsely by God's name, you profane God's name.
Do not profane the name of your God.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ תִשָּׁבְע֥וּ בִשְׁמִ֖י לַשָּׁ֑קֶר וְחִלַּלְתָּ֛ אֶת־ שֵׁ֥ם אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You must not defraud your neighbor or rob him. You must not withhold until morning the wages due a hired hand.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people to act justly toward others.
You must not cheat your neighbor.
You must not steal from your neighbor.
You must pay a hired worker his wages on time.
You must not keep a worker’s pay with you until morning.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תַעֲשֹׁ֥ק אֶת־ רֵֽעֲךָ֖ וְלֹ֣א תִגְזֹ֑ל לֹֽא־ תָלִ֞ין פְּעֻלַּ֥ת שָׂכִ֛יר אִתְּךָ֖ עַד־ בֹּֽקֶר׃

passages.text: You must not curse the deaf or place a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people.
God says, “Do not curse a deaf person.”
Do not put a stumbling block in front of a blind person.
Fear your God.
I am the LORD.
passages.original: לֹא־ תְקַלֵּ֣ל חֵרֵ֔שׁ וְלִפְנֵ֣י עִוֵּ֔ר לֹ֥א תִתֵּ֖ן מִכְשֹׁ֑ל וְיָרֵ֥אתָ מֵּאֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You must not pervert justice; you must not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the rich; you are to judge your neighbor fairly.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people to act justly.
Do not pervert justice.
Do not show partiality to the poor.
Do not show favoritism to the rich.
Judge your neighbor fairly.
passages.original: לֹא־ תַעֲשׂ֥וּ עָ֙וֶל֙ בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט לֹא־ תִשָּׂ֣א פְנֵי־ דָ֔ל וְלֹ֥א תֶהְדַּ֖ר פְּנֵ֣י גָד֑וֹל בְּצֶ֖דֶק תִּשְׁפֹּ֥ט עֲמִיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: You must not go about spreading slander among your people. You must not endanger the life of your neighbor. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God commands them.
Do not spread slander among your people.
Do not endanger your neighbor’s life.
I am the LORD.
passages.original: לֹא־ תֵלֵ֤ךְ רָכִיל֙ בְּעַמֶּ֔יךָ לֹ֥א תַעֲמֹ֖ד עַל־ דַּ֣ם רֵעֶ֑ךָ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You must not harbor hatred against your brother in your heart. Directly rebuke your neighbor, so that you will not incur guilt on account of him.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people to act with love and honesty.
Do not hate your brother in your heart.
If your neighbor does wrong, speak to him directly.
Do not keep silent about his sin.
If you do not correct him, you may share in his guilt.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תִשְׂנָ֥א אֶת־ אָחִ֖יךָ בִּלְבָבֶ֑ךָ הוֹכֵ֤חַ תּוֹכִ֙יחַ֙ אֶת־ עֲמִיתֶ֔ךָ וְלֹא־ תִשָּׂ֥א עָלָ֖יו חֵֽטְא׃

passages.text: Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against any of your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God commands His people.
Do not seek revenge against your people.
Do not hold a grudge against your people.
Love your neighbor as you love yourself.
I am the LORD.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תִקֹּ֤ם וְלֹֽא־ תִטֹּר֙ אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְאָֽהַבְתָּ֥ לְרֵעֲךָ֖ כָּמ֑וֹךָ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You are to keep My statutes. You shall not crossbreed two different kinds of livestock; you shall not sow your fields with two kinds of seed; and you shall not wear clothing made of two kinds of material.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel.
God said, “Keep My statutes.”
Do not breed your livestock with a different kind.
Do not plant your field with two kinds of seed.
Do not wear clothing made from two kinds of material.
passages.original: אֶֽת־ חֻקֹּתַי֮ תִּשְׁמֹרוּ֒ בְּהֶמְתְּךָ֙ לֹא־ תַרְבִּ֣יעַ כִּלְאַ֔יִם שָׂדְךָ֖ לֹא־ תִזְרַ֣ע כִּלְאָ֑יִם וּבֶ֤גֶד כִּלְאַ֙יִם֙ שַֽׁעַטְנֵ֔ז לֹ֥א יַעֲלֶ֖ה עָלֶֽיךָ׃פ

passages.text: If a man lies carnally with a slave girl promised to another man but who has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there must be due punishment. But they are not to be put to death, because she had not been freed.
passages.sermon:
A man may lie with a woman.
This woman is a slave girl.
She is promised to another man.
She has not been redeemed.
She has not been given her freedom.
There must be punishment for this act.
They must not be put to death.
She was not free.
passages.original: וְ֠אִישׁ כִּֽי־ יִשְׁכַּ֨ב אֶת־ אִשָּׁ֜ה שִׁכְבַת־ זֶ֗רַע וְהִ֤וא שִׁפְחָה֙ נֶחֱרֶ֣פֶת לְאִ֔ישׁ וְהָפְדֵּה֙ לֹ֣א נִפְדָּ֔תָה א֥וֹ חֻפְשָׁ֖ה לֹ֣א נִתַּן־ לָ֑הּ בִּקֹּ֧רֶת תִּהְיֶ֛ה לֹ֥א יוּמְת֖וּ כִּי־ לֹ֥א חֻפָּֽשָׁה׃

passages.text: The man, however, must bring a ram to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting as his guilt offering to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A man has sinned and is guilty.
He must bring a ram.
He must bring the ram to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
He must give the ram to the LORD as a guilt offering.
passages.original: וְהֵבִ֤יא אֶת־ אֲשָׁמוֹ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה אֶל־ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד אֵ֖יל אָשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: The priest shall make atonement on his behalf before the LORD with the ram of the guilt offering for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven the sin he has committed.
passages.sermon:
A priest stands before the LORD.
The priest takes a ram for a guilt offering.
The priest makes atonement for the man.
The man has sinned.
The priest offers the ram for the man’s sin.
God forgives the man for his sin.
passages.original: וְכִפֶּר֩ עָלָ֨יו הַכֹּהֵ֜ן בְּאֵ֤יל הָֽאָשָׁם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה עַל־ חַטָּאת֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֑א וְנִסְלַ֣ח ל֔וֹ מֵחַטָּאת֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָֽא׃פ

passages.text: When you enter the land and plant any kind of tree for food, you shall regard the fruit as forbidden. For three years it will be forbidden to you and must not be eaten.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to the Israelites.
You will enter the land.
You will plant trees for food.
You must treat the fruit as forbidden.
For three years, the fruit will be forbidden to you.
You must not eat the fruit during these three years.
passages.original: וְכִי־ תָבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־ הָאָ֗רֶץ וּנְטַעְתֶּם֙ כָּל־ עֵ֣ץ מַאֲכָ֔ל וַעֲרַלְתֶּ֥ם עָרְלָת֖וֹ אֶת־ פִּרְי֑וֹ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֗ים יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם עֲרֵלִ֖ים לֹ֥א יֵאָכֵֽל׃

passages.text: In the fourth year all its fruit must be consecrated as a praise offering to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God gave a law to Israel.
God commanded the people about fruit trees.
In the fourth year after planting a fruit tree, all its fruit is holy.
The people must set apart all the fruit as an offering.
The people must offer the fruit to the LORD as praise.
passages.original: וּבַשָּׁנָה֙ הָרְבִיעִ֔ת יִהְיֶ֖ה כָּל־ פִּרְי֑וֹ קֹ֥דֶשׁ הִלּוּלִ֖ים לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit; thus your harvest will be increased. I am the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for when they entered the land.
God told them to plant trees for food.
God said, "In the fifth year, you may eat the fruit of the tree."
God promised, "If you do this, your harvest will increase."
God said, "I am the LORD your God."
passages.original: וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֗ת תֹּֽאכְלוּ֙ אֶת־ פִּרְי֔וֹ לְהוֹסִ֥יף לָכֶ֖ם תְּבוּאָת֑וֹ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: You must not eat anything with blood still in it. You must not practice divination or sorcery.
passages.sermon:
God gave these commands to Israel.
God is the LORD.
Do not eat anything that still has blood in it.
Do not practice divination.
Do not practice sorcery.
passages.original: לֹ֥א תֹאכְל֖וּ עַל־ הַדָּ֑ם לֹ֥א תְנַחֲשׁ֖וּ וְלֹ֥א תְעוֹנֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: You must not cut off the hair at the sides of your head or clip off the edges of your beard.
passages.sermon:
God gave these commands to the people of Israel.
God is the LORD.
Do not cut off the hair at the sides of your head.
Do not clip off the edges of your beard.
passages.original: לֹ֣א תַקִּ֔פוּ פְּאַ֖ת רֹאשְׁכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֣א תַשְׁחִ֔ית אֵ֖ת פְּאַ֥ת זְקָנֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: You must not make any cuts in your bodies for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God says, “I am the LORD.”
Do not make any cuts in your body for the dead.
Do not put tattoo marks on yourselves.
passages.original: וְשֶׂ֣רֶט לָנֶ֗פֶשׁ לֹ֤א תִתְּנוּ֙ בִּבְשַׂרְכֶ֔ם וּכְתֹ֣בֶת קַֽעֲקַ֔ע לֹ֥א תִתְּנ֖וּ בָּכֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You must not defile your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will be prostituted and filled with depravity.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God commands fathers.
Do not defile your daughter.
Do not make your daughter a prostitute.
If you do this, the land will become corrupt.
The land will be filled with depravity.
passages.original: אַל־ תְּחַלֵּ֥ל אֶֽת־ בִּתְּךָ֖ לְהַזְנוֹתָ֑הּ וְלֹא־ תִזְנֶ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ זִמָּֽה׃

passages.text: You must keep My Sabbaths and have reverence for My sanctuary. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God commands them to keep His Sabbaths.
God commands them to show reverence for His sanctuary.
God says, "I am the LORD."
passages.original: אֶת־ שַׁבְּתֹתַ֣י תִּשְׁמֹ֔רוּ וּמִקְדָּשִׁ֖י תִּירָ֑אוּ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You must not turn to mediums or spiritists; do not seek them out, or you will be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God is the LORD your God.
Do not turn to mediums.
Do not turn to spiritists.
Do not seek them out.
If you seek them, you will become defiled by them.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּפְנ֤וּ אֶל־ הָאֹבֹת֙ וְאֶל־ הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֔ים אַל־ תְּבַקְשׁ֖וּ לְטָמְאָ֣ה בָהֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: You are to rise in the presence of the elderly, honor the aged, and fear your God. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God commands you.
God is the LORD.
You must stand up when you see an elderly person.
You must show honor to old people.
You must fear your God.
passages.original: מִפְּנֵ֤י שֵׂיבָה֙ תָּק֔וּם וְהָדַרְתָּ֖ פְּנֵ֣י זָקֵ֑ן וְיָרֵ֥אתָ מֵּאֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: When a foreigner resides with you in your land, you must not oppress him.
passages.sermon:
A foreigner may come to live with you.
He may live in your land.
You must not oppress the foreigner.
You must not mistreat him.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יָג֧וּר אִתְּךָ֛ גֵּ֖ר בְּאַרְצְכֶ֑ם לֹ֥א תוֹנ֖וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You must treat the foreigner living among you as native-born and love him as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God commands them to treat the foreigner living among them as a native-born citizen.
God commands them to love the foreigner as they love themselves.
God reminds them that they were once foreigners in the land of Egypt.
God declares, "I am the LORD your God."
passages.original: כְּאֶזְרָ֣ח מִכֶּם֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם הַגֵּ֣ר׀ הַגָּ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֗ם וְאָהַבְתָּ֥ לוֹ֙ כָּמ֔וֹךָ כִּֽי־ גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: You must not use dishonest measures of length, weight, or volume.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God gave them laws to follow.
God said, “Do not act unjustly in judgment.
Do not cheat with measurements.
Do not use dishonest measures of length.
Do not use dishonest weights.
Do not use dishonest measures of volume.”
passages.original: לֹא־ תַעֲשׂ֥וּ עָ֖וֶל בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט בַּמִּדָּ֕ה בַּמִּשְׁקָ֖ל וּבַמְּשׂוּרָֽה׃

passages.text: You shall maintain honest scales and weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God gave them laws to follow.
God said, “You must use honest scales.
You must use honest weights.
You must use an honest ephah.
You must use an honest hin.
I am the LORD your God.
I brought you out of the land of Egypt.”
passages.original: מֹ֧אזְנֵי צֶ֣דֶק אַבְנֵי־ צֶ֗דֶק אֵ֥יפַת צֶ֛דֶק וְהִ֥ין צֶ֖דֶק יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: You must keep all My statutes and all My ordinances and follow them. I am the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God gave them statutes and ordinances.
God commanded the Israelites to keep all His statutes.
God commanded the Israelites to keep all His ordinances.
God commanded the Israelites to follow all His statutes and ordinances.
God said, “I am the LORD.”
passages.original: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־ כָּל־ חֻקֹּתַי֙ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ מִשְׁפָּטַ֔י וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃פ
